PertMind: Eliciting Emergent Biological Reasoning in LLM via Reinforcement Learning on Cellular Perturbation Data

Same direction matrix and same transforms as our previous entry. The only change is how the 27
panel targets absent from the K562 genome-wide screen are filled.

Those rows used to be a signed intersection of two Perturb-seq lines (same-sign evidence
averaged, conflicts zeroed). They are now the mean of unit-normalised response rows from every
reference screen that measured the target, rescaled to the norm the signed intersection would
have produced. The rescaling is deliberate: the ranking metric is a per-row cosine and cannot
see amplitude at all, while the log-fold-change error metrics can, so we change direction only
and leave amplitude where it was already measured.

Validated by simulating orphanhood on held-out receptor lines: delete the donor rows for 28
targets the donor does cover, refill by each strategy, and score exactly those rows. Four
independent draws, all positive on every receptor, bootstrap interval excluding zero. On the
two receptors sharing no assay lineage with the fill sources -- the conservative reading --
the multi-source mean gained +0.253 normalised perturbation-discrimination on the refilled
rows, i.e. +0.023 over the full 300 panel.

Three results we did not expect:

A single best source is WORSE than the shipped two-line intersection (-0.071). The gain is not
a better reference line; it is the averaging itself.

Sign-only voting across sources buys almost nothing (interval includes zero). The plain mean of
unit rows is what works -- the opposite of what sign-based gating elsewhere would suggest.

A constant fallback row scores 0.42 pooled and 0.38 on one receptor, BELOW the 0.5 a
non-informative row should earn, because a constant sits systematically closer to the wrong
targets than a random direction does.

All computed from public perturbation screens and the provided control cells. No manual
per-target curation.

Three stacked changes on the v3.6 base, each validated on a 3-line leave-one-line-out harness (RPE1/HepG2/Jurkat; same 300-pert panel, none is a source in the stack, so no leakage). (1) EXACT EMISSION: each perturbation drew its own 400 control cells while cell_eval2 scores with control_source=real, making the subset-vs-full control composition an information-free noise vector on every predicted delta that never cancels; measured at 0.425-0.446 of per-pert residual, correction removes 96.5%. (2) STRING graph smoothing at lambda 0.25, k=20, score>=700 -- the optimum moves from 0.4 to 0.25 once the emission fix is applied. (3) ANTI-SHARE 0.5 on the consensus, row norms restored. Anti-share alone is a losing trade (pds up, nmae/reach down) and graph smoothing is its mirror image; paired, each covers the other's cost. Cross-line OVERALL delta vs base: +0.0105 RPE1, +0.0091 HepG2, +0.0161 Jurkat, mean +0.0119, positive on 3/3 and single-peaked in the anti-share strength on each line independently.

Restores the orion-floor5-w025 configuration (dispersion 0.15). Gate deltas near the detection limit do not transfer reliably in sign.
